scope: Theorem 2.1 of the manuscript “Thermal FK–Ising interfaces and massive SLE” (preprints/Thermal-FK-Ising-interfaces-and-massive-SLE-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c2a2a4a8b4213752), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every (Ω, a, b, m) as above, there is a curve law µΩ,a,b,m such that, for every sequence with mesh tending to zero and satisfying all the preceding domain, marked Carathéodory, angle and nome assumptions, L(χδ ◦ γδ) =⇒ χ∗µΩ,a,b,m in the metric (2.5), along the full sequence. The physical prime-end curve law µΩ,a,b,m is indepen- dent of the lattices, admissible domain approximations and nome sequence. For m > 0, µΩ,a,b,m is the unique law in Definition 2.3. For m < 0, it is the reversal of the positive-mass law in (Ω, b, a) with mass |m|, with primal and dual boundary labels interchanged. In either case we call it thermal massive SLE16/3.
